{{Short description|Application of economic analysis to demography}}
{{cleanup rewrite|date=June 2022}}
{{Economics sidebar}}
'''Demographic economics''' or '''population economics''' is the application of [[economic]] analysis to [[demography]], the study of human [[Population (human biology)|population]]s, including [[population size|size]], [[population growth|growth]], [[population density|density]], [[population distribution|distribution]], and [[vital statistics (government records)|vital statistics]].<ref name="economic demography">{{cite dictionary |doi=10.1057/9780230226203.0428 |entry=Economic Demography |title=The New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics |year=2008 |last1=Kelley |first1=Allen C. |last2=Schmidt |first2=Robert M. |isbn=978-0-333-78676-5 |page=655 |location=London |publisher=Palgrave Macmillan}}</ref><ref>{{cite dictionary |pmid=12342564 |first=Bernard M. S. |last=van Praag |author-link=Bernard van Praag |journal=Journal of Population Economics |jstor=20007247 |year=1988 |title=The notion of population economics |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=5–16 |doi=10.1007/bf00171507}}</ref>

{{Further|Econography}}

== Subareas ==
The ''[[Journal of Economic Literature]]'' classification codes are a way of categorizing subjects in economics. There, demographic economics is paired with [[labour economics]] as one of [[JEL classification codes|19 primary classifications]] at JEL: J.<ref>Of which a complete list for JEL: J with corresponding Wikipedia links is at [[JEL classification codes#Labor and demographic economics JEL: J Subcategories]].</ref> It has eight subareas:
: General
: Demographic Trends and Forecasts
: [[Family economics|Marriage; Marital Dissolution; Family Structure]]
: [[Family economics|Fertility; Family Planning; Child Care; Children; Youth]]
: Economics of the Elderly; Economics of the Handicapped
: Economics of Minorities and Races; Non-labor Discrimination
: Economics of Gender; Non-labor Discrimination
: [[Value of life]]; Foregone Income
: Public Policy
